---
title: "PDDL"
subtitle: "The domain file, the problems zeno writes, and plane goals"
---

MultiZenoTravel was designed as a benchmark for multi-objective temporal planners. `zeno pddl`
writes any instance as a PDDL 2.1 problem for the domain in `pddl/`, with its exact front as
comments, so that a planner's output can be scored against the true front.

## The domain

`pddl/multi-zeno-travel.pddl` (PDDL 2.1 level 3: durative actions and numeric fluents), as it
stands in the repository:

{{< include _pddl-domain.md >}}

- `fly` lasts `(timeTerre ?from ?to)`. Its only condition is that the plane is at `?from` at the
  start, and it adds `(citythreat ?to)` to `total-cost` when it lands.
- `board` and `debark` are instantaneous, and `(libre ?a)` holds while plane `?a` is empty, which
  enforces capacity one.
- The metric minimises `total-time` and `total-cost` together.

## Problems

```sh
zeno pddl [instance options] [-O FILE] [--no-front]
```

The default file name is `zeno<n>n<t>t<p>pMulti.pddl`. A complete example, for $n = 2$, $t = 2$,
$p = 1$ (durations $(2, 1)$, costs $(1, 2)$):

{{< include _pddl-problem.md >}}

- `city0` is $C_I$, `city1`…`cityN` the central cities, `city(N+1)` is $C_G$; `citythreat` is the
  landing cost, 0 for both hubs.
- `timeTerre` is written for both orders of every pair: $d_i$ between $C_I$ and $i$, $\bar d_i$
  between $C_G$ and $i$, and $\max(d_i, \bar d_i) + \max(d_j, \bar d_j) + 100$ between two central
  cities. Central flights are never faster than through a hub, so every problem satisfies (A1)
  when symmetric and (A1-NS) otherwise. They are written for every pair, so the file is quadratic
  in $n$.
- Every person and every plane starts in $C_I$, and the goal puts all of them in $C_G$.
- The trailing comments list the durations (both sides when non-symmetric), the costs, and, for a
  symmetric instance without `--no-front`, the Pareto front as `makespan cost` lines. Note the
  order: makespan first, the reverse of `zeno front`'s `cost makespan`.

## Plane goals {#plane-goals}

The goal requires every **plane** to end in $C_G$ as well as every person. Problem files written
before plane goals were added (pull request #9) only constrain the persons: planes may end
anywhere, and the makespan is the last arrival. For symmetric instances under (A1) that variant
has the same front ([Theorem 4.5](../proofs.qmd#node-theorem-4-5), machine-checked), so the fronts
in old files remain valid. The Lean checker covers it too, for certificates of version 1
(`Cert.check_sound_anywhere`).

## Makespan semantics {#semantics}

`board` and `debark` take no time in the model. Under the ε-separation of PDDL 2.1, a planner's
plan with $k$ actions on its critical path ends at $M + O(k\varepsilon)$, where $M$ is the sum of
the flight durations on that path. ZenoSolver reports $M$, the makespan in the limit
$\varepsilon \to 0$. Revision 2 of the note argued the correspondence in both directions (its
Statement 1.2, a sketch); revision 3 removed it, and §1.3 of the note now describes the encoding and
claims nothing about PDDL plans. The fronts of the note are those of the plans of its model
([Theorem 4.5](../proofs.qmd#node-theorem-4-5), [Corollary 5.6](../proofs.qmd#node-corollary-5-6)),
a model that abstracts the domain (§1.3 of the note).
Whether PDDL planners and VAL accept zero-duration actions is not checked.

## Size

The writer is quadratic in $n$, because of the central flights: about $2n^2$ `timeTerre` lines.
On an Apple M4 Max, a problem with $n = 1000$ is written in 0.36 s and takes 46 MB. Without
`--no-front`, `zeno pddl` also solves the instance first, which adds its solve time
([size guidance](sizing.qmd)).
